# Safety board simulation (generated by `python -m rnd.safety_board_sim`)

2026-11-28. Method: **ngspice /usr/bin/ngspice** for the analog decks; the board logic is an event-driven python model of the electrical.md netlist (v3). Astra review #3, critical 3: *simulate the board before power*. A model of an unbuilt board: it decides what to build and what the bench measures ([safety_board_tests.md](safety_board_tests.md)); it is not evidence the board works.

## 1. Regen clamp dump: bus overshoot at the drives

Board VBUS (C1 4.7 mF, C2 10 µF film, SMDJ33A, 1 kΩ bleeder, 3 × NH-50 0.56 Ω + 1 µH, VS-40CPQ060 freewheel, IRFB7530 VDMOS, R_G 4.7 Ω, UCC27524, TLV3202 as a hysteretic switch with its delay) → harness (fuse, XT60s, 14/16 AWG pairs at 60 °C, 0.6 µH/m) → each drive's 470 µF + its regen as P(t)/V. Corners: ± 1 % on both thresholds (TL431B + 0.1 % divider). Variants: *v3 as drawn* (on 27.0 / off 25.8 V, comparator straight on the divider); *proposed* (on 26.0 / off 25.7 V, 2 µs divider filter, 50 µs minimum on-time).

Nodes: T = shoulder pitch drive (end of the bench lead / lift umbilical), R = roll (after the pitch spiral and the detach plug), Y = yaw, E = elbow drive + node, W = DM-J4310. Limits: drive ≤ 28 V − 0.5 V = 27.5 V (GIM6010 12–28 V); MOSFET drain ≤ 48 V (80 % of 60 V); the lowest drive voltage is shown for the ESR dips; the off threshold at the low corner must clear a full pack (> 25.4 V); NH-50 ≤ 312 J per pulse (25 % of the 5 s overload rating).

**What it shows.** (1) **As drawn, the clamp rings at MHz:** the clamp's turn-on pulls the board node down by ≈ 146 A × C1's ESR plus the film capacitor's sag (≈ 2 V), more than the 1.2 V hysteresis window, so the 55 ns TLV3202 switches straight off, the node jumps back, and it switches on again at the gate-edge rate (the simulation aborts on it; on the bench: MOSFETs in linear mode, overheating). The old 36 µs TLV3702 hid this. Fix: a 2 µs RC on the divider and a 50 µs minimum on-time (one SN74LVC1G123 on OV ↑, ORed into the gate): the chopper then runs at a few kHz. (2) **The board's threshold is not the drive's voltage:** regen current flows from each drive to the board through ≈ 0.1 Ω of fuse, connectors and 14/16 AWG, so the elbow sits 1–3 V above the board. With v3's window (on at 27.0 V ± 1 %) the drives exceed 27.5 V already at ≈ 330 W; on at **26.0 V** (0.3 V hysteresis; ± 1 % still clears a full pack, lowest drive ≥ 26 V at the low corner) buys ≈ 1 V. (3) Even then the bus can take only the regen power below, so the full simultaneous peak-torque stop (1.3 kW per arm) overshoots: controlled stops must stay under it (drive limits at rated, peak-limit tests one joint at a time, a planner decel limit), or the branch needs a lower resistance / a local clamp.

| Bus | Regen power with every drive ≤ 27.5 V (proposed board, high corner) | Worst-case need (all joints at peak) | Rated-limit stop (×0.45) |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | **611 W** | 1328 W | 598 W ✅ |
| robot | **1663 W** | 2767 W | 1245 W ✅ |

| Case | PRE_OK after | K1 closes | ΔV at closing → making current | Inrush (K2 + R3) | Energy in R3 | |

| M1, K1 operate 25 ms, idle ×1.0 | 59 ms | 84 ms | 1.63 V → 60 A | 7.5 A | 2.4 J | ✅ |
| robot, K1 operate 25 ms, idle ×1.0 | 128 ms | 153 ms | 2.50 V → 136 A | 7.5 A | 4.4 J | ⚠️ |
| M1, K1 operate 5 ms, idle ×1.0 | 59 ms | 64 ms | 2.60 V → 99 A | 7.5 A | 2.4 J | ✅ |
| robot, K1 operate 5 ms, idle ×1.0 | 128 ms | 133 ms | 2.79 V → 152 A | 7.5 A | 4.4 J | ⚠️ |
| robot idle draw ×1.5 (0.90 A) | never (bus 22.1 V, 3.0 V short) | PRE_TIMEOUT at 1 s, K2 opens | – | 7.5 A | 5 J (rating 1250) | ✅ |
| M1 with a 10 Ω dummy load | never (bus 18.4 V, 6.7 V short) | PRE_TIMEOUT at 1 s, K2 opens | – | 7.5 A | 17 J (rating 1250) | ✅ |

PRE_OK needs the bus's total idle draw under 0.91 A (3 V across 3.3 Ω, before the ±0.25 V of comparator tolerance): the robot's 15 drivers at the 40 mA ESTIMATE draw 0.60 A, plus the 12 V DC-DC and the nodes downstream of the contactor; at ×1.5 (0.90 A) the robot never reaches PRE_OK. **Board test T3 measures the real idle draw; the robot needs R3 ≤ 2.2 Ω (with a relay rated for the 11.5 A inrush) if its idle draw is over ≈ 0.8 A.** K1's making current (ΔV left at closing over ≈ 20 mΩ) is 60–100 A on M1 and 136–152 A on the robot: check the ALEV100 make rating, or close K1 on a tighter PRE_OK once the idle draw is known.

The watchdog tolerance is the largest term: at +20 % the 25 ms monostable alone is 30 ms. That is why the review says *K1 open ≤ 30 ms* does not follow from the part value: it is 32 ms from the last edge to WD_OK low, before the contactor moves. The board test measures the monostable (T5) and the release (T4) separately and the bench test the end-to-end time, independently of any software timestamp.

| ARM with a mushroom pressed / without heartbeat | v3 as drawn | LATCH False / False | ✅ |
| logic supply lost and restored (PSU trip, brownout) | v3 as drawn | after power returns: LATCH False, K1 open (power-on reset) | ✅ |
| mushroom tapped (coil loop broken for 0.5 ms) while armed | v3 as drawn | LATCH False, K1 open | ✅ |
| AUX wire breaks while running | v3 as drawn | no FORCE (U6 is held cleared: K2_DRIVE = LATCH ∧ ¬AUX goes high and K2 re-closes), K1 stays closed on PRE_OK: a latent fault; the next stop gets **no forced discharge** (≈ 300 ms of bus on the drives' idle draw). Only the Pi sees it (AUX_OK low → supervisor e-stop latch) | ❌ |
| AUX stuck closed, then ARM | v3 as drawn | K1 closes on an empty bus (pre-charge bypassed: Q4 holds on AUX, K2_DRIVE = ¬AUX is off), bus 0.0 V at closing → inrush limited only by ESR / wiring; and no aux edge at the next stop, so no FORCE | ❌ |
| K1 main contacts welded, heartbeat stops | v3 as drawn | no aux edge → no FORCE; the bus stays powered from the supply; only the Pi (DISABLE frames) and the drives' CAN timeout remain | ❌ |
| 12 V gate-driver supply lost (U2 / F2) while running | v3 as drawn | the comparator still switches but UCC27524 has no supply: no clamp, no FORCE, and K1 stays closed. Regen then charges the bus without limit (M1 1.3 kW into 7 mF: 25 → 28 V in ≈ 0 ms) | ❌ |
| heartbeat stops while running | v3 + fixes | K1 open 33.2 ms after the last edge (wd 25 ms + release), FORCE yes, heartbeat back → K1 stays open | ✅ |
| ARM with a mushroom pressed / without heartbeat | v3 + fixes | LATCH False / False | ✅ |
| logic supply lost and restored (PSU trip, brownout) | v3 + fixes | after power returns: LATCH False, K1 open (power-on reset) | ✅ |
| mushroom tapped (coil loop broken for 0.5 ms) while armed | v3 + fixes | LATCH False, K1 open | ✅ |
| AUX wire breaks while running | v3 + fixes | discrepancy → FORCE at +30 ms and LATCH cleared, K1 open at +40 ms (the clamp loads the supply for the release time: the bench supply may latch); stop, fail-safe | ✅ |
| AUX stuck closed, then ARM | v3 + fixes | ARM refused (¬AUX on the ARM condition) | ✅ |
| K1 main contacts welded, heartbeat stops | v3 + fixes | FORCE 53 ms after the last edge: the clamp loads the supply at 135 A → the bench supply latches off (≥ 43.8 A); on the robot the pack keeps the bus up: needs a second break (BMS discharge FET off) | ✅ |
| 12 V gate-driver supply lost (U2 / F2) while running | v3 + fixes | 12 V UVLO → STOP: K1 opens, LATCH cleared (the bus then has no clamp: the 1 kΩ bleeder and the SMDJ33A only) | ✅ |

## Design changes from this simulation

0. **Clamp comparator: 2 µs RC on the divider + a 50 µs minimum on-time** (one more SN74LVC1G123 on OV ↑, ORed with OV and FORCE before the UCC27524). As drawn the clamp's own turn-on step at the board node is larger than its hysteresis and it rings at MHz (section 1). **Thresholds: on at 26.0 V, off at 25.7 V** (was 27.0 / 25.8 V as the corners were computed): ± 1 % still clears a full pack and every drive gains ≈ 1 V.
1. **Q4 (K1 coil driver) → 100 V logic-level MOSFET** (e.g. an IRL540N-class part, V_GS(th) ≤ 2 V, R_DS(on) specified at 4–5 V; drive it from the UCC27524's spare channel at 12 V if no 100 V part is specified at 3.3 V). With D1 + Z1 across the coil the drain sees supply + V_Z + V_F ≈ 50 V at every turn-off; the IRLB8721 is a 30 V part. Q5 (K2) likewise ≥ 60 V.
2. **ARM needs AUX open:** U10's D input becomes S1b ∧ S2b ∧ WD_OK ∧ TH1 ∧ ¬AUX. A stuck-closed AUX (welded aux, shorted opto) otherwise lets K1 close straight onto an empty bus (Q4 holds on AUX, K2_DRIVE = ¬AUX never pre-charges) and removes the opening edge that fires FORCE.
3. **K1 discrepancy monitor:** coil command (Q4 gate) ≠ AUX for > 30 ms (longer than the 25 ms operate time) fires FORCE and clears LATCH (an XOR, an RC and a comparator into U6's trigger and U10's CLR̄). It catches a welded K1 (coil off, AUX closed: the clamp loads the bench supply at ≈ 135 A, which latches it off, so power is removed without software), a broken AUX wire (coil on, AUX open: as drawn K2 re-closes, U6 is held cleared and the next stop has no forced discharge) and a K1 that fails to close. On the robot the pack keeps a welded bus up: the robot also needs a second break (BMS discharge MOSFET off over CAN / its enable input) on the same stop.
4. **12 V supervision:** a 10.5 V UVLO comparator on the gate-driver supply in series with WD_OK (or U2's power-good into U8): without the 12 V the clamp and FORCE are dead while the contactor can still close.
5. **Regen at the drive, not just at the board:** the board clamps its own node; each drive sits behind its harness resistance, so regen current lifts it above the board. The branch limits above are a requirement on the drive torque limits and the planner (≤ that regen power per branch during a controlled stop), and the bench scopes the bus **at the drive** (T8). If a joint needs more, it needs a thicker branch or a local clamp.
6. **Branch fuse vs the in-arm 16 AWG:** a 20 A slow-blow leaves the clock-spring 16 AWG unprotected from ≈ 18 A to ≈ 35 A (it may take minutes at 22–30 A; section 4), and a 15 A fuse still leaves ≈ 20 A for up to 600 s (and is under 1.25 × the arm's 14.8 A sustained). The fuse stays 20 A for shorts; overloads get a **branch current monitor**: a Hall sensor per arm branch on the board (ACS724-30A class) → 5 s RC → comparator at 16 A → STOP (into U10's CLR̄, latched). Needed before the arm's own harness is powered (Step 2); Step 1 (≤ 13.8 A peak on a 14 AWG lead) is protected by the 20 A fuse and the supply latch as it is.
